title: Twenty-One ₹100-Crore Films. One Man. Akshay Kumar Just Rewrote Bollywood History.
excerpt: Welcome to the Jungle crossed ₹100 crore in nine days, giving Akshay Kumar a record no other Indian actor is even close to touching — and the franchise that started 19 years ago just proved it's indestructible.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Akshay Kumar has achieved ₹100-crore grossers 21 times, a record unmatched by any Indian actor.
  • Welcome to the Jungle crossed ₹100 crore in just 9 days, showcasing strong box office performance.
  • The film earned ₹30 crore from overseas markets, highlighting its appeal among the Indian diaspora.
  • Akshay's latest film is his fourth consecutive ₹100-crore grosser, the longest active streak post-pandemic.
  • The Welcome franchise, starting 19 years ago, continues to thrive with its comedic charm.

The number is almost absurd. Twenty-one.

That's how many times Akshay Kumar has delivered a ₹100-crore net grosser at the Indian box office — a feat no other actor in Indian cinema has achieved. Not Shah Rukh Khan. Not Salman Khan. Not Ajay Devgn. Nobody.

And the film that got him there? A comedy about lovable idiots causing chaos in the wilderness. Of course it was.

Welcome to the Jungle, the third installment in the beloved *Welcome* franchise, crossed the coveted ₹100-crore mark on its second Saturday, Day 9, with a powerful 67% jump that pushed its India tally past ₹105 crore. By Sunday, with another commanding ₹9.44 crore, the film was sitting at ₹113 crore net domestically and ₹165 crore worldwide after just 10 days.

For a comedy entertainer released in the sweltering June heat — no holiday window, no festival weekend — those are numbers that demand respect.

The Welcome DNA

> **"## The Record Nobody Else Can Touch

Twenty-one films in the ₹100-crore club."**

Director Ahmed Khan understood the assignment. The *Welcome* franchise has never been about reinventing the wheel. It's about turning the wheel so hard it flies off, hits someone in the face, and makes everyone laugh. Akshay Kumar, Suniel Shetty, Paresh Rawal, and Arshad Warsi are the quartet that defined a generation of Bollywood comedy, and seeing them back together — this time joined by Disha Patani, Raveena Tandon, and Jacqueline Fernandez — is the kind of nostalgia that opens wallets.

The film opened to a solid ₹19.4 crore on Day 1 and roared past ₹65 crore in its first weekend. The first week closed at ₹95 crore, setting up a tense race toward the century.

Surviving Alpha

Then came the real test. On Day 8, Alia Bhatt and Sharvari's Alpha arrived, and the screen count for *Welcome to the Jungle* dropped from 9,917 to 7,557 — nearly 2,400 screens gone overnight. Most second-week films would have cratered.

*Welcome to the Jungle* barely flinched. It collected ₹4.50 crore on its second Friday, dipping less than 20% despite the brutal screen crunch. Then Saturday happened: ₹7.50 crore, a 67% jump, and the century was officially crossed. Sunday added another ₹9.44 crore — the kind of hold that makes multiplex programmers quietly shift showtimes back in the comedy's favour.

The audience had already decided what it wanted to watch.

The Record Nobody Else Can Touch

Twenty-one films in the ₹100-crore club. Let that register.

This is Akshay's fourth consecutive ₹100-crore grosser — the longest active streak for any Bollywood actor in the post-pandemic era. It's his seventh century in the post-pandemic era alone, the highest for any Indian actor. His last six releases have all cleared ₹100 crore worldwide: *Sky Force*, *Kesari Chapter 2*, *Housefull 5*, *Jolly LLB 3*, *Bhooth Bangla*, and now this.

The man has been written off a dozen times over. "Overexposed." "Too many films." "Needs to be more selective." And yet here he is, stacking centuries like Virat Kohli in a home series — except nobody is bowling at him; they're just booking tickets.

Where the Diaspora Showed Up

Here's the number that matters most to NRIs watching from abroad: ₹30 crore from overseas markets in 10 days. The *Welcome* franchise has always occupied a special place in the diaspora — it's the kind of slapstick, no-subtitles-needed comedy that plays at family gatherings from Edison to Southall. This third installment is no different.

The film is still running in theatres across the US, UK, Canada, and Australia. If you haven't caught it yet, it's exactly the kind of two-hour escape a July evening calls for — no plot summary required, just turn off your brain and enjoy Paresh Rawal doing what he does best.

What Comes Next

*Welcome to the Jungle* is tracking toward a ₹135–145 crore net lifetime in India, depending on how it holds against Dhamaal 4 and Ikka — both arriving July 10. Worldwide, ₹200 crore is within striking distance.

For a franchise that started 19 years ago with Akshay Kumar, Nana Patekar, and Anil Kapoor causing chaos at a gangster's mansion, that kind of longevity is its own form of star power.

Akshay Kumar doesn't need a spy universe or a superhero cape. He just needs a gang of good actors, a script that doesn't take itself too seriously, and an audience that knows exactly what it signed up for.

Twenty-one. Count them.
